name: What is the difference between a design-build firm and a general contractor?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a design-build firm and a general contractor for custom home construction?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a design-build firm and a general contractor for custom home construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: A design-build firm and a general contractor can both deliver a custom home, but they work differently. In a design-build setup, the design and construction teams are coordinated under one roof or one process, which can simplify communication, budgeting, and scheduling. In a general contractor model, the architect and engineer usually complete the plans first, and then the contractor builds from those documents. Design-build can help homeowners make decisions earlier and catch budget issues sooner. A traditional general contractor arrangement can offer more separation between design and construction, which some homeowners prefer. In Los Angeles, either approach can work well if the team is experienced and transparent. The better choice depends on how much design control the homeowner wants, how complex the site is, and whether early budgeting or independent design is the priority. What matters most is whether the team communicates clearly and understands local building conditions.
acceptedAnswer.description: A design-build firm manages design and construction under one coordinated team, while a general contractor usually builds from completed plans created by separate designers. Design-build can simplify communication and scheduling, while a separate GC model can offer more independence between design and construction.
